findings.title: Failed partial submit releases registry lock before revoking already-submitted worker
findings.mechanism: The second _EXECUTOR.submit can raise inside with _REGISTRY.lock. Unwinding first releases the lock, and only the outer except reacquires it to set batch.failed and close children. A waiting first worker can win that interval; its guard sees the whole binding and both RUNNING records, failed=false, while record2.future is still None. The comment promising no guard passage until complete submission or revocation is false.

reproducer.method: Real service/AIAgent/executor/handler. Fault-inject second submit RuntimeError; main-thread line trace yields at _release_contract line515, after unlock and before exception cleanup. This forces a legal scheduler interleaving without replacing worker/guard/handler results.
reproducer.positive: Same script first executes the exact same stage through real release: SUCCEEDED, two executions, both futures done.

findings.violated_requirement: H04/§5 fail-closed pre-access batch barrier; task explicitly requests partial-submit races and handling of both records. No work may escape the incomplete submission barrier advertised by _release_contract.
findings.minimal_remedy: Catch submission failure and latch batch.failed/UNKNOWN/revoke both children inside the SAME registry-lock critical section before unlocking. Preserve running futures; do not wait/join under the lock. Keep an interleaving regression that asserts zero reader/handler entries after second-submit failure.
findings.limits: No cross-task data was returned and no final was fabricated here; UNKNOWN/no retry remain intact. Only finite PURE local work escaped the partial-submit barrier, not target IO. Scheduler cut is deterministic fault injection, not a frequency estimate.

findings.title: Failure publishing the second record leaves the first publicly ready/SUCCEEDED in an UNKNOWN batch
findings.mechanism: The success loop publishes record.result one record at a time. If result construction/hashing/dataclasses.replace fails on record2, the except handler changes record.state to UNKNOWN but never clears already-published record.result. Public service.result(handle) prefers record.result, so record1 remains ready=True/terminal_state=SUCCEEDED while both registry states and the whole batch are indeterminate.

reproducer.method: Both real child futures settle successfully; inject a failure in dataclasses.replace on the second SubagentResult publication. Read exact service.result handles and batch readback after the outer failure handler.
reproducer.positive: Same service release channel succeeds with two complete results without the fault.

findings.violated_requirement: Homogeneous whole-batch publication only after settlement; on failure/UNKNOWN do not retain or publish partial success, and treat both records consistently.
findings.minimal_remedy: Construct/hash the full set of SubagentResult objects before publishing any. Ensure failure rollback of result/completed state is performed within the same publication lock before any reader can observe partial publication; keep batch indeterminate and preserve futures. Regression must inspect public result(handle), not only record.state and batch readback.
findings.limits: The main managed RPC batch readback correctly refuses; this reproduces a leak through the existing native lifecycle result surface, not persisted API acceptance. Fault seam models a publication exception/BaseException cut; no claim of normal dataclasses.replace randomly failing.

findings.title: Both batch2 variants return before the shared strict observation/forbidden-effect oracle
findings.mechanism: The batch2-stop-first and batch2-release-first branches return at5658/5770. finally runs cleanup, but the strict observation/readiness/forbidden-* checks at7563–7574 are ordinary code after finally and are skipped. release-first only checks access counts/times and real AIAgent rows; stop-first only checks absence of read/handler/run_contract. Unknown/malformed observer rows or a caught forbidden attempt can therefore coexist with branch success. launch_bootstrap_checkpoint in finally records diagnostics but does not enforce them.

reproducer.method: Compile/execute the unchanged source assertion window5700–5728 only, with explicitly synthetic same-channel events. AST confirms both early-return sites. No PG test import/execution or DB/OCI effects.
reproducer.positive: A valid two-read/four-handler overlap plus two REAL_AIAgent observations is accepted.

findings.violated_requirement: H04/H08 and QA contract require same-channel fail-closed observer evidence, zero forbidden attempts, and unknown evidence not silently accepted. User specifically requested reporting safety-relevant signals hidden by the new PG oracle.
findings.minimal_remedy: Apply the existing common bounded/strict observer-readiness and forbidden-event refusal checks on both batch2 exits, preferably once in shared post-cleanup logic, while keeping task-count-specific assertions separate. Do not weaken the singleton oracle. Add same-channel caught-forbidden and unknown-row negatives, then run the two separately authorized PG/native variants.
findings.limits: PG/native variants were not executed. This is a verified source-oracle defect with synthetic events, not proof that a forbidden native effect occurred in a live PG run.

lesson_for_parent_skill_update: On a locked multi-submit barrier, catch and latch revocation before exiting the submission lock, not in an outer except. Failure tests must inspect the public per-record result as well as state/batch readback. Early returns inside try/finally skip any safety oracle after finally; challenge new branches with a caught forbidden event on the same channel. No skill file modified by this read-only reviewer.
